question: Choose the indirect form of the given sentence: He said, "I shall do my best."
options: He said that he would do his best.
He said that I would do his best.
He said that he would do my best.
He said that I shall do my best.
correct_answer: He said that he would do his best.
explanation: In indirect speech, the pronoun 'I' changes to match the subject ('he'), and the modal 'shall' changes to 'would' when reporting in past tense.

question: Choose the right answer from the five options given below to frame a meaningful sentence: Rama / garden / in / the / be / may

question: Choose the indirect form of the given sentence: I said, "The teacher likes me."
options: I said that the teacher liked me.
I said that the teacher was liking me.
I said that the teacher likes me.
I said that the teacher is liking me.
correct_answer: I said that the teacher liked me.
explanation: Simple present tense in direct speech changes to simple past tense in indirect speech: 'likes' becomes 'liked.'
